propositions: When two bundle objects exist for a single ref in S3, git-remote-s3's push rejects all writes and clone fails with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', making the store unclonable and push retriable but non-convergent.

Upstream's interactive Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is unusable for autonomous fleets (blocking input() prompts crash on EOF) and discards the non-chosen head's unique events into an orphan ref, causing data loss unacceptable in an append-only event log.

S3-specific multi-bundle state is ordinary ref divergence at the bundle-storage layer; rebar already solves the divergence case via sync's lossless 2-parent merges that union heads and require git-merge conflict for refusal, so the doctor reuses that exact reconcile logic.

The heal must write the merged-bundle tip as a durable NEW object before deleting any original bundles and never delete the merged tip, ensuring at every crash point ≥1 bundle carrying the full merged history remains remotely.

The heal acquires the helper's per-ref S3 lock (IfNoneMatch conditional-put with 60s TTL and stale-lock steal) to serialize concurrent repairs; a backing-off process relies on the winner's collapse to a single bundle, converging on the next push retry within the same call.
